title: Turn your ChatGPT chats into apps with the Glide MCP server
summary: Your plans, lists, and drafts already live in ChatGPT. Connect it to GlideOS with the Glide MCP server, and they become apps your team can sign in to and use.
body_markdown:
Think about the last useful thing you worked out in ChatGPT. Maybe it was a cleaned-up customer list, a checklist for new hires, or a plan for how jobs should move from quote to invoice.


It's probably still sitting in that chat. To use it, someone has to copy it into a spreadsheet, a doc, or an email. Then the details change, and that copy goes stale.


[Glide's Model Context Protocol (MCP) server](https://www.glideapps.com/docs/os/mcp) closes that gap.


Connect ChatGPT to your GlideOS account, and the same chat can build a working app from what you've already written. GlideOS, our AI-first platform for business apps and agents, then runs it, with hosting, a database, sign-in, permissions, and team access.


You don't need to write code or know how any of this works under the hood. If you can describe what you want in a chat, you can build with it.


*Use Claude? We covered that setup in[Claude builds it, GlideOS runs it](https://www.glideapps.com/blog/claude-glideos-mcp-server) .*


## What happens after the chat ends?


ChatGPT is good at the thinking part. It works out what you need, drafts it, and fixes it when you push back. What it can't do on its own is keep that result running for your whole team next week.


That's the job GlideOS does.


Connected through the Glide MCP server, ChatGPT works as you, inside your GlideOS organization, and can only open the projects you can. What it builds lives in GlideOS: the apps, the tables behind it, and the rules for who sees what.


## How do you connect ChatGPT to GlideOS?


*The Glide MCP server is included on the GlideOS Pro plan and above.[Get started for free](https://os.glideapps.dev/) , then upgrade your organization to Pro.*


The Glide MCP server creates a secure connection between ChatGPT and your GlideOS account. All you need is the Glide MCP server address:


```text
https://mcp.glideapps.dev/mcp
```


Once it's connected, ChatGPT can see your projects and make changes, but only the ones you're allowed to make. You set it up once, and it's there in every chat after that.


### In ChatGPT on the web


*Note: You'll need a paid ChatGPT plan to add a custom MCP connection.*


1. Go to[chatgpt.com/plugins](https://chatgpt.com/plugins) , select **+** , and choose **Add custom MCP server** .
2. Name it GlideOS and paste the address under **Server URL** .
3. Set authentication to **OAuth** , read OpenAI's standard warning about connecting outside tools, and select **I understand and want to continue** .
4. Select **Create as a plugin** , install it, and sign in with your GlideOS account. GlideOS then asks you to approve the connection. If you belong to more than one organization, you pick one here, and ChatGPT stays connected to that one. To switch, reconnect.
5. Start a new chat, type **@** , pick GlideOS, and ask it to list your projects. If it can, you're connected. If ChatGPT later stops with an error about reading Glide's guidance, refresh or reconnect GlideOS in ChatGPT.


Paste one address, sign in once, and GlideOS is there in every chat.


On ChatGPT Business or Enterprise, a workspace admin controls who can add custom MCP servers, and can publish GlideOS for the whole workspace. Each person still signs in with their own GlideOS account.[Learn more about it in the ChatGPT docs](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/12584461) .


The same address and sign-in work with Claude and other MCP clients.


Matching settings live on the **Agents** screen in GlideOS.


## What can ChatGPT actually do in GlideOS?


The Glide MCP server gives ChatGPT the same abilities as any other MCP client. Here's what it covers, in roughly the order customers use them:


- **Build and fix apps:** make changes, preview them, and check for errors. *"Add a required photo field to the job form."*
- **Answer questions about your data:** ask in plain English, and ChatGPT looks it up in your database. *"How many orders came in last week?"*
- **Publish and undo:** push changes live, see past versions, and roll back.
- **Run calculations behind the scenes:** *"Recalculate the totals on every open invoice."*
- **Use integrations:** find the integrations available to your organization and run actions through them.
- **Automate with workflows:** jobs that run on a schedule, or when something happens, like a form being submitted.
- **Back up your data:** take a snapshot before a risky change.


It can handle setup, too. ChatGPT can create or find a project, import a spreadsheet or other source into tables, and set an app's name, icon, and color. It can claim a web address or connect your own domain, and choose who gets in: only members of your organization, anyone who signs up, sign-in optional, or fully public.


## What does this look like for a small business?


Many ChatGPT users already have the makings of an app in their chat history: a job list they pasted in to clean up, a checklist they drafted, a sales question they ask every week. With GlideOS connected, those chats can become tools your team uses every day.


Here are six everyday jobs to try. Start each request with **@GlideOS** so ChatGPT knows to use it:


1. **Turn a chat into a tool.** You drafted a new-hire checklist in ChatGPT last month. *"Turn the onboarding checklist from this chat into an app where each new hire ticks off their steps, and I can see who's done."*
2. **A phone app for your crew (trades and field services).** Start from the spreadsheet you already run jobs from. *"Here's my jobs sheet. Turn it into an app my crew can use on their phones, staff only."*
3. **A client portal on your own domain (agencies, accountants, clinics).** *"Build a portal at portal.ourfirm.com where clients sign in to check the status of their own file."*
4. **Quick answers from your sales data (retail and restaurants).** The questions you already ask ChatGPT, answered from your real numbers. *"What were my 10 best sellers last month?"* or *"Which items are below par right now?"*
5. **A weekly report that sends itself.** *"Every Monday at 8, email me last week's open jobs."* Connect Gmail in GlideOS first. Reports can also start when something happens, like a new form submission.
6. **A safety net before changes.** *"Back up my data, then add a discount field to orders."* If something breaks: *"Roll back to the last version."*


From a checklist in ChatGPT to an app your new hires use.


### Already building in GlideOS?


GlideOS has its own built-in agent, but ChatGPT is still useful, because a lot of your planning already happens there. For example: The notes from a chat about next quarter can turn straight into app changes.


It works on apps you already run, too:


- **Fix a problem:** *"Why does the Overdue tab show jobs that are finished?"*
- **Understand an app:** *"Walk me through how the reminder workflow works, step by step."*
- **Clean up data:** *"Find duplicate customers and show them to me before changing anything."*
- **Add features carefully:** *"Add a status filter to the jobs list and let me preview it before you publish."*


Each teammate connects their own ChatGPT and gets only their own access. If someone can't open a project in GlideOS, they can't reach it through ChatGPT either.


## Is it safe to let an AI loose in my business?


Handing an AI the keys to live business data is a fair thing to be nervous about.


Here's what keeps ChatGPT in check:


- **Access mirrors yours.** ChatGPT signs in to your GlideOS organization as you, with the projects and features available to your account.
- **You control approvals.** Set which Glide actions require approval, and review ChatGPT’s approval prompt when one appears. Whether ChatGPT prompts can also depend on its settings and the action.
- **Take a snapshot before experimenting.** If a change causes trouble, you can roll back to a snapshot.
- **Some tasks stay manual.** Inviting guests, for example, is still done in the GlideOS dashboard.


When ChatGPT asks for approval, you see exactly what it's about to change.


Approve the actions you've read, not the ones you skimmed.[OpenAI's own docs](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/developer-mode) point out that a wrong write action can change or delete data, which is why backups matter.


## Ready to try it?


1. Add` https://mcp.glideapps.dev/mcp` as a custom MCP server in ChatGPT.
2. Sign in with your GlideOS account.
3. Ask something like *"@GlideOS, turn this Excel spreadsheet into a dashboard for my team."*


Already on GlideOS Pro? Try it on an app you run today, and ask ChatGPT to back up first.
